However, there is precedent for a sixth Great Lake to be established. In 1998, the federal government designated Lake Champlain between New York and Vermont as a Great Lake, but that only lasted about two weeks after states bordering the original five Great Lakes objected. (3/🧵)

On this day 38 years ago, President Clinton designated Lake Champlain as the 6th U.S. Great Lake. This passed as a part of a bill that reauthorized the National Sea Grant Program and allocated specific funding for Great Lakes research. (1/2)
